summary: This Artinis Medical Systems blog post, written by Sophie Apprich and dated August 9, 2023, explains why functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) suits sensitive participants such as children, infants, the elderly and clinical populations. It describes the technique's non-invasiveness, short set-up time, tolerance of movement and wearable portability, and surveys research applications in older adults and in infants and toddlers. It also presents Artinis solutions such as BabyBrite optodes, neoprene headcaps and lightweight devices under 300 g.
one_line: Artinis blog post arguing fNIRS is well suited to monitoring the brain of sensitive participants like infants and the elderly, with examples and product features.
key_facts: fNIRS is a non-invasive neuroimaging technology measuring relative concentration changes in oxygenated and deoxygenated hemoglobin that reflect brain activity in local cortical regions.
The blog post states fNIRS can be applied to subjects of any age, skin color, or condition, including sensitive participants such as children, the elderly, or the clinical population.
fNIRS is less prone to movement artifacts than other neuroimaging technologies such as EEG and fMRI.

Dual Task paradigms, usually simultaneous conduction of a motor task (e.g. walking) and a cognitive or executive task (e.g. arithmetic calculation), are frequently used to assess cognitive function in the elderly.
Vitorio R et al. (2021) studied changes in prefrontal cortical activity and turning in response to dopaminergic and cholinergic therapy in Parkinson's disease in Parkinsonism Relat Disord.
The BabyBrite is specifically designed for babies aged from 0 to 1.5 years and comes with flat optode tips and extra soft optode holders made from biocompatible materials.
Artinis headcaps and headbands are made of neoprene, which shields external light to minimize its influence on data quality.
Generally, all Artinis portable devices weigh less than 300 g.
Hyperscanning, meaning simultaneous fNIRS measurement in multiple subjects, is often used in developmental psychology studies of social interaction of infants and toddlers with caregivers or peers.
Xie S et al. (2021) examined executive function in bilingual young children using fNIRS in International Journal of Bilingualism.
Lai Y et al. (2020) studied whether tennis benefits the updating function in young children, published in Applied Sciences.
Sun F et al. (2022) reported a protocol for a game-based high-intensity interval training program on executive function of children with ADHD.
Germain C et al. (2022) studied the effect of physical activity level on prefrontal cortex hemodynamics in older adults during single- and dual-task walking in J Aging Phys Act.
Pellegrini-Laplagne M et al. (2022) studied acute effects of simultaneous exercise and a cognitive task on executive functions and prefrontal oxygenation in healthy older adults in Brain Sci.
Optode holders for portable fNIRS devices come in three different heights to help ensure accurate skin-optode contact and easy hair removal.
